question: _________, built by the Mughal Emperor Shah Jahan in the 17th century, was the main residence of the Mughal Emperors for nearly 200 years.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Red Fort, Delhi**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Emperor Shah Jahan commissioned the construction of the Red Fort on** 12 May 1638**.
 
• The Mughal state's **formal and political centre** was the Red Fort in Delhi.
 
• Shah Jahan erected the Red Fort when he chose to transfer his imperial **headquarters from Agra to Delhi**.
 
• The Red Fort was created to serve as the abode of the Royal Mughal families and was named** Quila-E-Mubarak**.
 
• **Nahar-e-Bahisht** is the most beautiful creation in the Red Fort.
 
• Red fort is the fusion of the **Timurids and the Persian** architectural styles.
 
• **Ustad Ahmad Lahauri** was the architect of the Red Fort.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information __**

__
 
• **Tughlaqabad Fort**-Tughlaqabad Fort is a ruined fort in Delhi built by** Ghiyas-ud-din Tughlaq**, founder of the **Tughlaq dynast**y.
 
• **Siri Fort**, in the city of New Delhi, was built during the rule of **Alauddin Khalji**, the second ruler of the Khalji Dynasty.
 
• **Salimgarh Fort** was built in **1546** AD in Delhi on a former land of the** Yamuna River by Salim Shah Suri son of Sher Shah Suri**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **About Shah Jahan**.

 
 
• **Shah Jahan (1592-1666)** was the** fifth Mogul emperor** of India.
 
• The third son of Emperor **Jahangir**, Shah Jahan was born in Lahore on** Jan5,1592**.
 
• Shah Jahan successfully ruled the empire for **30 years**.
 
• Shah Jahan was an able administrator and commander.
 
• He is best known for the construction of the ***Taj Mahal*** which he built in memory of his beloved wife** Mumtaz Maha**l.
